title: Systemic Coverage Diagnostics, Golden Proof & SMB-08 Handoff
objective: Complete the MSWI family by interpreting accepted PCA-12/PDCP Packet-08 graph/run evidence into permission-safe systemic coverage diagnostics, proving the full reduced family and absorbed residual obligations through the automated golden battery, validating exact-head/provider-off operation, and producing a non-authoritative SMB-08 capability handoff without inventing mechanics to improve diagnostic scores.
acceptance: Coverage diagnostics interpret accepted PCA-12/Packet-08 graph/run evidence without creating a second generic simulation or formal-analysis runtime.
Diagnostics report declared fan-out, loops, dead routes, duplicated routes and missing integrations without inventing routes or mechanics to improve scores.
Permission filtering precedes diagnostic counts, graph/tabular projections, search, explanation, AI context and export; hidden connectivity cannot leak through aggregate metadata.
Accessible semantic/text/tabular alternatives cover every blocking diagnostic and golden-proof result without dependence on graph visuals, color, animation or audio.
The automated family golden battery proves all sealed surviving MSWI contracts plus absorbed owner residual obligations required by the durable family DCP.
Exact-head Linux, hosted Windows and deterministic cross-platform validation prove provider-off operation and optional-AI independence.
Golden proof preserves target-owner authority, bounded fan-out, Campaign-time semantics, uncertainty classes, stable identity/history, explicit promotion and all sealed predecessor boundaries.
SMB-08 handoff is capability evidence only and grants no implementation authority or canonical owner mutation.
No paid/cloud provider is required for any blocking diagnostic, proof or handoff workflow.
boundaries: MSWI-01, MSWI-03, MSWI-04, MSWI-06, MSWI-07 and MSWI-14 plus all upstream completed programs remain sealed.
PCA-12 and PDCP Packet-08 retain generic simulation/formal-analysis authority; MSWI-18 owns only MSWI graph interpretation, coverage diagnostics and family proof.
Diagnostics describe declared connectivity and gaps; they never invent mechanics, routes or integrations to improve a score.
Permission-safe diagnostics cannot expose hidden route/population/site/component metadata through counts or aggregate topology.
MSWI-18 is the reduced family golden gate; successful closeout may only create the roadmap-authorized SMB-08 handoff/selection state determined from fresh dependency authority.
No successor may be started by MSWI-18 closeout without the ordinary OPS3 governed-start rule.
